UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist (Geologist): questions by topic, 2014–2026

2851 questions from 52 papers — the whole exam a Geologist candidate sits. 1171 mains parts and 840 prelims Geology items, classified against the Geologist syllabus; 840 prelims General Studies items, classified against the Paper I syllabus. Marks are rescaled to what each paper actually carries, so any year is comparable with any other.

EVIDENCE Both prelims papers are here because both count towards the cut-off that admits a candidate to mains: Paper I is General Studies, 120 items for 100 marks, and Paper II is Geology/Hydrogeology, 120 items for 300 marks. Paper I carries the fewer marks and none of them count in the final ranking, but a candidate who misses its cut-off never reaches the mains papers at all — so it is reported here in full, and separately, rather than mixed into the geology weightage.

Trend analysis and forecast for the next paper — year-wise and topic-wise breakdowns, trends, repeated concepts, projected weightage and a preparation plan, each with the arithmetic behind it.

A predicted question paper for CGS 2027 — a full prelims Paper II and three mains papers, constructed from the recurrences documented here. Constructed, not leaked: read the disclaimer on that page first.

EVIDENCE The question text below is machine-extracted from the scanned PDFs UPSC published. Where a paper was a photocopy, OCR damage survives in the text; 162 of 2851 items could not be classified at all and are grouped as Unclassified rather than being forced into a topic. The PDFs in this folder remain the authority.
